records.title_en: Offshore wind may be good for the climate but can it be good for the ocean, too?
records.summary_zh: 海上风电在全球可再生能源网建设中日益普及，但其对海洋环境的影响引发关注。研究表明，风电场可禁止底拖网等有害捕捞，起到事实上的海洋保护区作用，但同时也对鸟类和蝙蝠构成威胁，并可能对海洋环流和温度产生未知影响。专家指出，行业需持续投资与创新，以在推进低碳转型的同时缓解生态负面影响。
records.summary_en: - Offshore wind energy is on the rise. Many experts regard it as pivotal to building renewable energy grids around the globe, while also noting that it affects the marine environment. - On one hand, offshore wind farms can create mini marine protected areas by prohibiting harmful practices like bottom trawling, and could eventually enable restoration of depleted habitats like oyster reefs. - But they also bring notable challenges. Alongside well-documented threats to birds and bats, several issues remain poorly understood, such as how large-scale wind platforms might affect ocean circulation, temperature and the movement of sediment. - Researchers say a host of measures can be taken to address some environmental challenges, while underlining the need for continued investment and innovation in solutions.

records.title_en: The datacenter fight could permanently transform US politics. Which party will seize advantage?
records.summary_zh: 美国各地因大型科技公司的数据中心建设引发广泛反对，居民对水资源消耗和空气污染表达强烈不满。目前四分之三的美国人反对本地开发数据中心，超过 500 个县和市镇通过了禁令或暂停令，这一议题正对美国跨党派政治产生深远影响。
records.summary_en: The movement against datacenters are uniting Americans because they perfectly illustrate how a few individuals hold all the power to control decisions that impact our lives Bryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade. The lead organizer with Citizens Action Coalition (CAC), a consumer and environmental organization, he usually encounters a mix of reactions when he’s out canvassing; whatever issue he’s talking about, there’s always at least a few people on the other side. But at a recent festival in the rural town of Monrovia, Indiana, he was struck by an unusual spirit of unity. He was there about a proposed datacenter , a 550-acre (222-hectare) Google project in this small town of 1,600 people. “I had 50 people I talked to,” Gustafson told me. “Nobody wanted that datacenter in their community. And at least a half a dozen people came up to me to say, ‘Hey, I voted for Trump. What the heck’s he doing, supporting these things?’” Continue reading...

records.title_en: Two planned datacentres will have higher UK carbon emissions than ExxonMobil, analysis finds

records.title_zh: 巴西独特的数据中心热潮依托清洁电力，但也带来社会负担
records.title_en: Brazil’s unique data center boom rides on clean power despite social burden
records.summary_zh: 由于可再生能源过剩导致严重的弃电损失，巴西大批清洁能源企业转向投资建设大型数据中心以消化剩余电力。然而，近八成规划建设的园区与传统社区土地重叠，引发了公众对水文循环和生物多样性等潜在工业风险的担忧。
records.summary_en: - An exclusive analysis found at least 36 renewable energy companies have pivoted toward building massive server hubs to cash in on excess generation. - Nearly 80% of slated districts overlap with traditional lands where communities are unaware of industrial risks to hydrological cycles and biodiversity. - Government officials marketed the country’s green matrix to global investors while leveraging the power surplus in high-stakes trade talks with the United States.

records.title_zh: 风电盈余助长了巴西干旱土地上不受监管的数据中心
records.title_en: Wind energy surplus fuels unregulated data centers in Brazil’s dry land
records.summary_zh: 巴西可再生能源公司 Serena 已提交 12 项申请，计划在巴伊亚州仅有 11,000 居民的偏远城镇热蒂奥杜欧鲁建设数据中心。该项目利用当地的风电盈余，但由于缺乏针对性监管，这些数据中心绕过了环境许可审批，给当地水资源和社区带来了生态压力。
records.summary_en: - The energy firm Serena filed 12 requests to build data centers in a remote town of only 11,000 people already affected by wind farms in Brazil. - The project sits in a protected area, stressing the waters of the Itaparica Lagoon, local fishers and Quilombola communities. - Tech firms in Brazil are exploiting a lack of specific regulations and renewable power surplus to plan data centers without undergoing environmental licensing.

records.summary_en: Exclusive: Planning documents show annual emissions from North Ockendon project would be equivalent to 8,480 flights to New York A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 8,480 flights from London to New York, planning documents show. The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”. Continue reading...

records.title_en: “Dangerous consequences” – how AI’s climate framing lets Big Tech off the hook
records.summary_zh: 前微软经理霍利·阿尔派恩指出，人工智能对气候的真正威胁不仅在于耗电巨大的数据中心，更在于其在化石燃料行业的广泛应用。科技巨头和国际能源署往往用 AI 优化可再生能源等绿色应用来掩盖温室气体排放增加，而实际上 AI 正在油田帮助化石能源企业更快、更廉价地开采石油和天然气。
